sub_theme: Traditional Tales: The Three Little Pigs

lessons.title: Story Time: The Three Little Pigs (Full Telling)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify the three main characters and setting of the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at the front cover and predict the story.
lessons.main_activity: Read/tell the full story with expression and props (finger puppets), pausing to check understanding of characters.

differentiation.support: Use puppets to point to characters as named
differentiation.extension: Predict what might happen next before turning the page

lessons.assessment_notes: Note character/setting recall — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap the three pigs and the wolf together.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Counting the Three Little Pigs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count to 3 and match quantity to the story characters.
lessons.starter_activity: Count 3 claps, 3 jumps together.
lessons.main_activity: Children count out groups of 3 objects representing the pigs, and practise counting other small quantities up to 5.

differentiation.extension: Extend counting practice to 5 with the same method

lessons.assessment_notes: Note accurate counting to 3+ — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class count-along to 3 with actions.
lessons.home_link: Count 3 objects together at home.

lessons.title: Straw, Sticks, and Bricks: Comparing Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the strength of straw, sticks, and bricks.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel/handle real straw, sticks, and a brick (or picture).
lessons.main_activity: Children test blowing on straw, sticks, and (imagine) a brick, predicting and observing which is hardest to move/break.
resources_needed: Straw, sticks, brick or heavy block
key_questions: Which material is easiest to blow away?

differentiation.support: Adult leads the test, child observes

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early scientific reasoning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap which material was strongest and why.
lessons.home_link: Look for materials at home and guess which would be strongest for building.

lessons.title: Building the Three Little Pigs' Houses
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to construct a simple model house using a chosen material.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the three house types in the story.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children build model houses using straw (raffia), sticks (lolly sticks), or bricks (blocks), then test blowing on each.

differentiation.extension: Compare and explain why one house was stronger

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe construction and design choices — evidence for EAD.1/UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Test all houses with a 'wolf' fan/blow and discuss results.
lessons.home_link: Build a simple house model at home with any materials available.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'h'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'h' and blend words (hot, hat, hen).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sounds learned so far.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'h' sound/action; blend new CVC words.
lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'h'.
lessons.plenary: Sing all 15 sounds learned.
lessons.home_link: Practise blending hot, hat, hen.

lessons.title: Positional Language: Huff and Puff
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional language describing the wolf's actions (blow down, knock at).
lessons.starter_activity: Act out 'huffing and puffing' together.
lessons.main_activity: Using small-world story props, children retell the blowing-down scenes using positional language.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note positional vocabulary use — evidence for MATHS.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap positional words used in the story retelling.
lessons.home_link: Use positional words describing objects at home.

lessons.title: Testing Air: Blowing and Wind
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe the effect of blowing air on different light objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Blow on a feather and observe.
lessons.main_activity: Children experiment blowing through straws at different light objects (paper, cotton wool, pom poms), observing which move most.
key_questions: What happens when you blow harder?

differentiation.extension: Compare and rank objects by how easily they moved

lessons.assessment_notes: Note investigative observation skill — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap what moved most and why.
lessons.home_link: Blow bubbles or a pinwheel together and discuss air force.

lessons.title: Role-Play: Three Little Pigs Story
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to act out a key scene from the story using expressive voices.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise a 'big bad wolf' voice and a 'little pig' voice.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children act out the 'knock, knock, let me in' and 'huff and puff' scenes using props/masks.
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe expressive language and confidence — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group performs for the class.
lessons.home_link: Act out the story with family using different voices.

lessons.title: Comparing Versions of the Three Little Pigs
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify one difference between two versions of the same story.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the traditional version read on Monday.
lessons.main_activity: Read/discuss a modern or alternative version (e.g. 'The True Story of the 3 Little Pigs') and compare to the original.
key_questions: What is different in this version?
Which version do you prefer? Why?

differentiation.extension: Explain differences in detail with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative comprehension — evidence for LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: Class vote on favourite version.
lessons.home_link: Ask a family member if they know a different version of a story you know.

lessons.title: Ordering the Story Events with Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to order story events using ordinal numbers (first, second, third).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the sequence of houses in the story.
lessons.main_activity: Children order picture cards of the three houses using ordinal number labels (first pig, second pig, third pig).
resources_needed: Story sequencing cards, ordinal number labels
key_questions: Which pig built the third house?

differentiation.extension: Use ordinal language independently for all 3

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ordinal number understanding — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of the story order using ordinal numbers.
lessons.home_link: Practise ordinal numbers with a simple sequence at home (e.g. lining up toys).

lessons.title: Real Pigs: Facts and Habitats
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name one fact about real pigs and where they live.
lessons.starter_activity: Compare the storybook pigs to real pigs (pictures).
lessons.main_activity: Discuss real pig facts (they live on farms, like mud, are intelligent animals) using picture/video resources.

differentiation.support: Share one simple fact with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual recall about real animals — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap real pig facts learned.
lessons.home_link: Look up a fact about a farm animal together.

lessons.title: Straw, Stick, Brick Texture Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use different textured materials to represent the three house types in a collage.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel each material sample again.
lessons.main_activity: Children create a triptych collage using real straw, small sticks, and painted 'brick' paper to represent the three houses.
resources_needed: Straw/raffia, small sticks, brick-pattern paper, glue
key_questions: Which material did you use for this house?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe material exploration and fine motor control — evidence for EAD.1/PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Display the three-house collages together.
lessons.home_link: Feel different textures around your home and describe them.

lessons.title: Writing Speech Bubbles for the Wolf and Pig
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a simple word/phrase for a character's speech.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap key phrases from the story ('let me in', 'not by the hair of my chinny chin chin').
lessons.main_activity: Children draw a character and attempt to write a simple word in a speech bubble (e.g. 'no' or 'in').

differentiation.extension: Independent phonetic attempt at a short phrase

lessons.assessment_notes: Note purposeful emergent writing — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share speech bubble writing with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Draw a character and their speech bubble at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Wolf and Pig Sizes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and describe size differences using comparative language.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at wolf and pig character size in the story pictures.
lessons.main_activity: Children compare cut-out wolf and pig figures, ordering by size and using comparative language.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative language accuracy — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of size comparisons made.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of toys or objects at home.

lessons.title: What Makes a House Strong? Recap Experiment
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to conclude which material makes the strongest house based on evidence.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Monday's material testing.
lessons.main_activity: Repeat/extend the blowing test on the three model houses built Monday, recording results with simple pictures/ticks.
resources_needed: Model houses from Monday, fan or straws for blowing

differentiation.extension: Child records own conclusions with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to draw simple conclusions from evidence — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class conclusion: bricks make the strongest house.
lessons.home_link: Test the strength of two different materials at home.

lessons.title: Composing a Wolf's Huff and Puff Song
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute to and perform a simple story-based song.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the story's key repeated phrases.
lessons.main_activity: As a class, create a simple chant/song about the wolf huffing and puffing to a familiar tune, then perform with actions.
key_questions: What sound does the wolf make?

differentiation.extension: Suggest a new line for the song

lessons.assessment_notes: Note creative contribution and performance confidence — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Perform the finished song together.
lessons.home_link: Sing the wolf song for family.

lessons.title: Retelling the Whole Story Independently
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the Three Little Pigs story with beginning, middle, and end.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about the story.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children retell the full story using puppets/props, supported by a story map.

differentiation.support: Retell with adult prompting at each stage

lessons.assessment_notes: Note full narrative retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group performs their retelling to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the whole story to your family this weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Ordinals, and Size
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting to 3, ordinal numbers, and size comparison skills from this week.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting pig figures, ordinal number sequencing, size comparison of characters.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 8 maths observations.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting and ordering over the weekend.

lessons.title: Materials Recap: What Would You Build With?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to justify a choice of building material using reasoning.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's material testing and conclusions.
lessons.main_activity: Children choose which material they would build their own house with and explain why, contributing to a class chart.
key_questions: Why is it a good choice?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to reason and justify — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class chart reveal of material choices.
lessons.home_link: Discuss what your home is built from and why it's a good material.

lessons.title: Three Little Pigs Performance Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to perform the story as a class with confidence, using props and song.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all elements learned this week (roles, song, houses).
lessons.main_activity: Whole-class performance of the Three Little Pigs story combining role-play, the huff-and-puff song, and the model houses as props.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of the story week?
How did it feel to perform?
lessons.assessment_notes: Observe confidence and enjoyment across the week's story learning — evidence for EAD.2/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause; recap the fun traditional tales week.
lessons.home_link: Perform part of the story for family this weekend.
